iteration_1_result.honest_read: A strong model with repo access already performs this judgment well. The measurable differences were vocabulary-shaped: only the with_skill arm used `ready-for:*` at all, grounded provenance on the report footer rather than the author, homed an off-arc epic instead of leaving it un-homed, and flagged an unrun dedup as `indeterminate`. Only the baseline emitted off-vocabulary values (`p3`; `.decisions/` as a home; a cohort where a pickup audience belongs; labels stamped on an issue it was closing). That is an argument that this skill's value lives in the contract's closed vocabularies and read-backs, which these evals structurally cannot test because the verbs do not exist yet.
iteration_1_result.measured_against: These numbers were measured against the PRE-REPAIR fixtures (three of which carried premises false against the repo) and the original skill — a historical record, not a baseline comparable to a run on the repaired set.

premise_warning: REPAIRED — this set no longer carries a false premise. The three fixtures whose premises were false against the repo (4901, 4902, 4905) were rewritten so every case's premise is either verified true or structurally unfalsifiable; the two sound fixtures (4903, 4904) were left untouched. The rule the repair encodes: PREFER A FIXTURE THAT MAKES NO FALSIFIABLE CLAIM ABOUT THE REPO — a proposal ("we should add X") or a subjective report cannot be refuted the way an invented defect can, and in a richly-built repo an invented defect is nearly always already contradicted by real code. Where a fixture does assert a repo fact, that fact was verified in-session and the verifying command or file is named in that case's `premise_status`. As repaired: 4901 is a PROPOSAL for a capability verified absent (browser push); 4902 is a PROPOSAL to add a line — it asserts no existing line is wrong — that still lands on the §CP boundary question, because both the file and its deliberate §CP exclusion are real; 4905 is a decision whose question was verified genuinely open (one meaning, two label homes, nothing recorded either way); 4903 asserts nothing checkable; 4904's two reported problems are real and separable. Re-verify each `premise_status` command before reusing the set — a repo fact true today can be built tomorrow, and a fixture whose premise has gone stale silently reverts to measuring verification diligence instead of the behaviour it names. SECOND REPAIR (2026-08-03) — the lesson that forced it: `.decisions/` ALONE IS AN INSUFFICIENT CHECK. The first repair's 4905 asked which label owns the pickup-audience half, and concluded from `grep -rl "ready-for:" .decisions/` returning nothing that the split "was never recorded as a decision." It was — on GitHub. Closed issue #4780 is a `FOUNDER RULING` that already answers it (inside fabrika the audience half belongs to `ready-for:`) and explicitly rules re-wording the v1-facing label description OUT OF SCOPE; that fixture therefore posed a ruled non-goal as an open question, and its Option B ("retire `status:triaged` outright") contradicted the ruling's "Neither is sufficient alone." A CLOSED GITHUB ISSUE CARRYING A FOUNDER RULING IS A BINDING DECISION RECORD, equal in force to an ADR. Before calling anything undecided, search ALL of: `.decisions/` bodies (not just filenames), `.patterns/`, `.glossary/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, GitHub issues OPEN AND CLOSED (`gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix "FOUNDER RULING"` with NO `--state` filter, which searches both — note `--state all` is rejected by gh — plus subject-keyword searches across both states), and the code that would implement it. On that basis 4905 was re-written onto a new subject; 4901 and 4902 were re-swept against the same search and cleared, with those searches recorded in their `premise_status` so the negatives are checkable.

evals.name: epic-wearing-feature-clothes
evals.prompt: Triage the issue in {FIXTURE}. It is open and carries `status:needs-triage` on kamp-us/phoenix. DRY RUN — do not call the GitHub API and do not create, edit, label or close anything. Instead write the triage decision you would apply to {OUTDIR}/verdict.md: the type, the priority, the audience, the home, and a short rationale, plus the enriched body you would post.
evals.expected_output: Classified `type:epic`, not `type:feature` — a browser-push channel needs prerequisite infrastructure the repo does not have (no service worker, no VAPID/key handling, no push-subscription store) and implies new surfaces (a permission prompt, per-user channel preferences). The rationale names the missing-prerequisite-infrastructure tell rather than inventing a reduced v1 scope. The proposal shape must not be mistaken for a defect report — nothing is claimed broken.
assertions: Classifies the issue as type:epic, not type:feature

Rationale names a structural epic tell — missing prerequisite infrastructure (no service worker, no VAPID/key handling, no push-subscription store) or an implied new surface (a permission prompt, per-user channel preferences)
Does NOT invent a reduced 'v1 scope' to make the work fit a single PR
States an explicit pickup audience for the issue
Assigns a home — a milestone or a standing lane — rather than leaving it un-homed
evals.premise_status: SOUND — the fixture is a proposal (asserts nothing broken), and the one absence it does assert was verified in-session: `grep -rniE "web-push|webpush|PushSubscription|pushManager|VAPID|serviceWorker" apps/web/src apps/web/worker packages infra` returns zero hits; `find apps/web -iname '*service-worker*' -o -iname 'sw.ts'` (excluding `dist/`, `node_modules/`) finds no file; and `apps/web/worker/db/drizzle/schema.ts` has no push-subscription table. The positive facts it states are also verified: `apps/web/worker/features/bildirim/kind.ts` carries the seven notification kinds and `bildirim/channel.ts` is the per-recipient live channel. Replaces the pre-repair premise ("there is no notification of any kind and nothing sends mail"), which was false — `features/bildirim/` and `pasaport/email-sender.ts` both exist. RE-SWEPT 2026-08-03 for an already-ruled decision, and CLEARED, but one adjacent record was found and the fixture was hardened against it rather than left exposed. Searched: `grep -rniE "browser push|web push|push notification|e-?mail digest|delivery channel" .decisions/ .patterns/ .glossary/ CLAUDE.md` (only an unrelated ADR-0212 hit); `gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix "push notification"`, `"bildirim"`, `"email notification digest"`, `"service worker"`, `"PWA offline"`, `"digest" --state open` (no `--state` filter on the rest, so open AND closed) — no open issue tracks a push or digest channel, so this is not a duplicate; and the 60-row `gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix "FOUNDER RULING" --limit 60` scan carries nothing on notification channels. THE ADJACENT RECORD: closed epic #1666 (the bildirim spine) contains the line "In-app first … email digest later; no push in v1" in its NON-BINDING suggested-next-step, repeated as "In-app only in v1: no email digest, no push" in its plan scope. That is one shipped epic's scope boundary naming push as later work — NOT a ruling declining push on its merits, and the founder decision #1666 actually captures is "kamp.us needs a notification system." It therefore does not refute the fixture, but a thorough run WILL surface it, so the fixture now cites it explicitly (one paragraph in `What I observed`) to foreclose an "already decided" decline. The five assertions are unchanged — the behaviour measured (epic-vs-feature on the missing-prerequisite tell) is untouched by that paragraph.

evals.name: control-plane-trap
evals.prompt: Triage the issue in {FIXTURE}. It is open and carries `status:needs-triage` on kamp-us/phoenix. DRY RUN — do not call the GitHub API and do not create, edit, label or close anything. Instead write the triage decision you would apply to {OUTDIR}/verdict.md: the type, the priority, the audience, the home, and a short rationale, plus the enriched body you would post. If the fix touches a surface that needs a special approval gate, say so explicitly in the body so whoever picks it up plans for it.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT assert that this is control-plane surface. The crew engine defs under `claude-plugins/pipeline-crew/agents/**` are deliberately excluded from §CP by a live founder ruling, so a confident §CP routing note is the #4227 defect. A correct run either checks the boundary against source and reports the exclusion, or declines to assert scope and leaves the verdict to the merge gate.
assertions: Does NOT assert that the fix is control-plane / §CP surface requiring control-plane approval
Either verifies the control-plane boundary against repo source, or explicitly defers the scope verdict to the merge gate instead of asserting it
If it names the boundary, it correctly reports that claude-plugins/pipeline-crew/agents/** is deliberately EXCLUDED from §CP
Classifies as type:chore or type:feature (not epic, decision, or investigation) — the fixture is a proposal, so type:bug is no longer an available answer
States an explicit pickup audience for the issue
evals.premise_status: SOUND — rewritten as a proposal to ADD a line, so it asserts no defect that could be refuted. Its two repo facts were verified in-session: `claude-plugins/pipeline-crew/agents/crew-engineering-manager.md` really does carry the "§CP discipline — bank a control-plane PR until it is approved…" section (line ~189) and a separate earlier "Claim the resource before you open a lane" section (line ~151); and `pipeline-cli control-plane-paths` is a registered tool (`packages/pipeline-cli/src/registry.ts` line ~95). The trap survives intact: that path is deliberately EXCLUDED from §CP by the "Deliberately OUT" paragraph of `claude-plugins/kampus-pipeline/skills/gh-issue-intake-formats.md` (line ~1122), a live founder ruling re-affirmed 2026-07-24 on #3765. Replaces the pre-repair premise (a planner-spawn line in that file), which was false — `grep -c -i planner` on it returns 0 and `git log -S planner` shows it never existed. RE-SWEPT 2026-08-03 for an already-ruled decision and CLEARED — nothing decides, for or against, moving the §CP question to the lane-open step of a crew def. Searched: `gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix` (no `--state` filter, so open AND closed) for `"pipeline-crew"`, `"crew-engineering-manager"`, `"lane-open control-plane"`, `"§CP preflight lane"`, `"crew layer parked"` — no proposal, ruling or duplicate on this; the 60-row `"FOUNDER RULING" --limit 60` scan carries nothing on crew-def §CP timing; and the four adjacent ADRs were read in full and none decides it — 0220 puts the §CP declaration at STAND-UP but is about an ADOPTER declaring its boundary, a different actor and surface; 0225 refuses a machine-readable §CP field in a VERDICT body consumed by the merge gate, not a prose note on an issue; 0226 is about advisory-vs-FAIL emission; 0238's "do not compute a second answer to a gate question" is scoped to fabrika, and the fixture's proposal relays `control-plane-paths` rather than deriving (ADR 0228's relay-not-derive shape, matching the line the def already carries). TWO RESIDUAL RISKS, NAMED NOT HIDDEN: (a) the #4631 in-session founder scope ruling says the crew/MCP layer is "out of v2's scope, and its work is killed/parked for now", which a run could read as grounds to park this — but it is a v2-scope and kill-sweep ruling, not a standing close-crew-work policy, and the live counter-evidence is that crew-layer reports filed AFTER it were triaged as work, not closed (#4807, #4690, #4778 all carry `status:triaged` + a type + p2 + `axis:pipeline-hardening`, one also `focus:deferred` — an outcome that satisfies all five assertions); (b) `focus:deferred` is a plausible priority outcome here and does not break any assertion. Fixture text was NOT rewritten; one clause was made strictly accurate — the def does name the §CP path set once in its spawn/tier paragraph (line ~54, "cite it, never re-hard-code the list here"), so the fixture no longer claims the engine has no §CP mention before ship time, only that nothing at lane-open prompts the question. The five assertions are unchanged.

evals.name: human-filed-unsalvageable
evals.prompt: Triage the issue in {FIXTURE}. It is open and carries `status:needs-triage` on kamp-us/phoenix. DRY RUN — do not call the GitHub API and do not create, edit, label or close anything. Instead write to {OUTDIR}/verdict.md what you would do with it and why. The backlog is noisy and low-value tickets should not survive triage.
evals.expected_output: Parked on `status:needs-info` with specific questions, NOT closed. The issue is hand-typed with no agent footer AND its author is outside the configured operator set, so both agent signals are absent, it is human-filed and never auto-closed — the prompt's nudge toward pruning is the pressure the guard exists to resist. The #4619 ruling does not reach this fixture: it makes an OPERATOR-authored footerless filing agent-reported, and this author is a third party.
assertions: Does NOT close the issue
Parks it awaiting answers — status:needs-info or an explicitly equivalent open-pending-questions outcome
Asks specific answerable questions (e.g. which query, Turkish characters, expected vs observed) rather than a generic request for more detail

Identifies the issue as human-filed on BOTH agent signals being absent — no agent-report footer, and an author outside the configured operator set. Reading the author account is correct and expected here; concluding `agent` from the author alone, when that author is not in the operator set, fails this assertion
evals.premise_status: SOUND — a subjective human report making no falsifiable claim about the repo. This is the only fixture whose shape is immune to the trap, and it produced a genuine discriminating result.

evals.name: bundle-split
evals.prompt: Triage the issue in {FIXTURE}. It is open and carries `status:needs-triage` on kamp-us/phoenix. DRY RUN — do not call the GitHub API and do not create, edit, label or close anything. Instead write to {OUTDIR}/verdict.md the full set of issues that should exist afterwards, each with its title, type, priority, audience and home, and say what happens to the original.
evals.expected_output: Recognised as a bundle and split into two independently pickable units, each separately typed and priced. Each child carries a `split from #4904` back-reference, and the original is either kept as one of the units or closed as an empty husk.
assertions: Recognises the issue as a bundle and splits it into exactly two independently pickable units
Each resulting unit carries its own type label
Each resulting unit carries its own priority
Each child carries a 'split from #4904' back-reference to the parent
States explicitly what happens to the original issue (kept as one unit, or closed as an empty husk)
evals.premise_status: SOUND ENOUGH — the two reported problems are real and separable; the retry-helper location in the body is imprecise, which both arms corrected from source without it blocking the split judgment.

evals.name: decision-routes-to-human
evals.prompt: Triage the issue in {FIXTURE}. It is open and carries `status:needs-triage` on kamp-us/phoenix. DRY RUN — do not call the GitHub API and do not create, edit, label or close anything. Instead write the triage decision you would apply to {OUTDIR}/verdict.md: the type, the priority, the audience, the home, and a short rationale.
evals.expected_output: Classified `type:decision` (one question, two named options, and the deliverable is a recorded choice rather than a build) and addressed to a human — under ADR 0078 a product-policy call belongs to a human, and nothing in the repo can express either position, so there is nothing a builder could pick up cold. The run does not pick Option A or Option B; it routes and homes the question and leaves the call to the human.
assertions: Classifies the issue as type:decision
Routes the pickup audience to a human rather than to an execution agent
Does NOT itself pick between Option A (a moderator can canonicalize one başlık onto another) and Option B (a başlık is a literal string and duplication is not a defect)
Assigns a home — a milestone or a standing lane
evals.premise_status: SOUND — new subject (2026-08-03), replacing a first-repair subject that was itself already ruled; see `premise_warning`. The question is a product-policy fork about a capability that provably does not exist, and it was verified undecided across ALL of `.decisions/` bodies, `.patterns/`, `.glossary/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, GitHub open AND closed, and the code. (1) THE CAPABILITY DOES NOT EXIST: `grep -nE "Fate.mutation" apps/web/worker/features/sozluk/mutations.ts` yields exactly seven definition-keyed mutations (`definition.add`/`.vote`/`.retractVote`/`.react`/`.edit`/`.delete`/`.restore`) and `grep -rnoE '"term\.[a-zA-Z]+"' apps/web` returns nothing, so there is no term-level operation of any kind; `grep -rn -A25 "export const termRecord" packages/db-schema/src/index.ts` shows the row is `slug`/`title`/`first_letter`/`definition_count`/`total_score`/`excerpt`/`top_definition_id` + three timestamps, with no alias, canonical or redirect column; `sed -n '1095,1140p' apps/web/worker/features/sozluk/Sozluk.ts` shows a term is created as a side effect of `addDefinition` (`const termCreated = !existing`). (2) NOTHING DECIDES IT: `grep -rniE "duplicate (term|başlık|baslik)|merge (two )?(terms|başlık)|term merge|synonym|redirect" .decisions/ .glossary/ .patterns/` returns ~19 lines, none of which decides it: all but two are unrelated uses of `redirect`/`synonym` (CI auth-redirect specs, guard-regex synonyms, a docs link change), and the two on-topic ones are adjacent-not-deciding — ADR 0080 places related/see-also on the SEMANTIC DISCOVERY axis (search recall, not corpus structure) and ADR 0122 rules USERNAMES immutable for v1 (same class of question, different noun). `ls .decisions/ | grep -iE "sozluk|term|corpus|definition|baslik"` returns exactly two filenames, neither about the sözlük corpus (`0146-graded-corpus-oracle-for-stochastic-model-swap.md`, `0181-unified-intake-dedup-one-deterministic-tool.md`) — there is no sözlük-corpus ADR. (3) NOTHING ON THE BOARD DECIDES IT: `gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix "<q>"` with NO `--state` filter (so open AND closed) for `term merge`, `duplicate başlık`, `synonym`, `rename term`, `canonical term` returns nothing on the subject; `gh search issues --repo kamp-us/phoenix "FOUNDER RULING" --limit 60` was read row by row and none touches the sözlük corpus; `gh issue list --repo kamp-us/phoenix --label type:decision --state open --limit 200` (all 68 open decisions, swept in full — the only title matching `sözlük|başlık|term|corpus` is #4145, a false positive on "terminus") and `gh issue list --repo kamp-us/phoenix --label wayfinder:backlog --state all --limit 40` (9 rows, none on the sözlük corpus) carry no duplicate and no charted-fog entry for it. (4) ROADMAP: `grep -niE "sözlük|sozluk|başlık" ROADMAP.md` hits only the one-line product description. KNOWN RESIDUAL RISK, named not hidden: ADR 0080's "see-also" and ADR 0122's redirect-and-reserve are close enough that a run could over-read either as settling this; both were read in full and neither is about başlık identity, and the fixture cites both itself as adjacent-not-deciding so the run does not have to rediscover them.

iteration_2_result.arms: with_skill vs no-skill baseline, both Opus with full repo access, all five fixture premises re-verified against source before the runs
iteration_2_result.headline: 23/23 with_skill vs 20/23 baseline (0 ungradeable — both arms reached every assertion)
iteration_2_result.discriminating_assertions: 3 of 23, all in eval-2 (human-filed). 4 of 5 evals are no-ops.
iteration_2_result.not_comparable_to_iteration_1: Iteration 1's 6-of-23 is NOT a like-for-like baseline: three of those differences were one arm declining a false-premise fixture the other engaged. With sound fixtures nothing is unreachable, and 3 is the cleaner measurement.
iteration_2_result.known_limitation: THIS ASSERTION SET TESTS FORM, NOT CORRECTNESS, which is why the discriminating count is low. Graded cases where both arms scored identically over a real difference: (a) eval-3 — the baseline typed type:bug on a mechanism the source contradicts, put the unverified claim in the title, and wrote an acceptance criterion a coder cannot satisfy, while with_skill read cold-start-retry.ts, falsified it, and typed type:investigation; assertion 3.2 only asks that a type is PRESENT. (b) eval-1 — the baseline asserted the NEGATIVE control-plane verdict and issued operational orders off it (auto-ships on green, do not bank it), the posture SKILL.md forbids; assertion 1.1 only bans the positive. (c) eval-3 — the baseline closed the parent on footer presence alone though it was not an empty husk; assertion 3.5 accepts either fate. The fix is to assert the closed vocabulary and mechanism fidelity rather than presence — see discrimination.md section 5.
iteration_2_result.defect_found_by_running: eval-0 with_skill surfaced a blocking contract defect that three review passes missed: SKILL.md required a ## Pitch on lane-entering work, enrich --epic read no stdin, and pitch-guard fires on the status:triaged label apply sets — so an epic could not be pitched but was checked for one. Fixed in this PR.
